views.name: delivered_orders_events
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  order_id,
  COALESCE(order_delivered_customer_date, order_delivered_carrier_date) AS delivered_at
FROM olist_orders
WHERE order_status = 'delivered'
  AND (order_delivered_customer_date IS NOT NULL OR order_delivered_carrier_date IS NOT NULL)
views.description: Select orders that are considered delivered, projecting the order identifier and the delivery timestamp/date used to determine delivery month and year. This filters to only rows whose status (or equivalent) indicates delivery.

views.name: delivered_orders_normalized_dates
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  doe.order_id AS order_id,
  CAST(strftime('%Y', doe.delivered_at) AS INTEGER) AS delivered_year,
  CAST(strftime('%m', doe.delivered_at) AS INTEGER) AS delivered_month
FROM
  delivered_orders_events AS doe
WHERE
  strftime('%Y', doe.delivered_at) IN ('2016','2017','2018')
views.description: Normalize the delivered_at timestamp into separate year and month components (integers). Keep only rows where the year is relevant for reporting (2016, 2017, 2018).

views.name: monthly_delivered_counts
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  don.delivered_year AS delivered_year,
  don.delivered_month AS delivered_month,
  COUNT(doe.order_id) AS delivered_count
FROM delivered_orders_normalized_dates AS don
LEFT JOIN delivered_orders_events AS doe
  ON don.order_id = doe.order_id
GROUP BY
  don.delivered_year,
  don.delivered_month
views.description: Aggregate counts of delivered orders per year and month. One row per (delivered_year, delivered_month) with the count of orders delivered in that bucket.

views.name: month_pivot_2016_2017_2018
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  m.delivered_month AS month_number,
  COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN m.delivered_year = 2016 THEN m.delivered_count END),0) AS delivered_orders_2016,
  COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN m.delivered_year = 2017 THEN m.delivered_count END),0) AS delivered_orders_2017,
  COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN m.delivered_year = 2018 THEN m.delivered_count END),0) AS delivered_orders_2018
FROM monthly_delivered_counts m
WHERE m.delivered_month BETWEEN 1 AND 12
  AND m.delivered_year IN (2016,2017,2018)
GROUP BY m.delivered_month
views.description: Pivot the monthly delivered counts so there is one row per calendar month (1..12) and separate columns for delivered_orders_2016, delivered_orders_2017, delivered_orders_2018. Ensure months with zero counts for a year appear as 0. Order of rows will be calendar January to December.

views.name: monthly_records
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  CAST(strftime('%Y', order_delivered_customer_date) AS INTEGER) AS year,
  CAST(strftime('%m', order_delivered_customer_date) AS INTEGER) AS month,
  COUNT(order_id) AS delivered_orders_volume
FROM olist_orders
WHERE order_status = 'delivered'
  AND order_delivered_customer_date IS NOT NULL
  AND strftime('%Y', order_delivered_customer_date) IN ('2016','2017','2018')
GROUP BY year, month
views.description: Select the monthly delivered-orders records restricted to the years 2016, 2017, and 2018. Keep one row per month record with its year, month, and delivered orders volume.

views.name: annual_delivered_per_year
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  monthly_records.year AS year,
  SUM(monthly_records.delivered_orders_volume) AS annual_delivered_orders_volume
FROM
  monthly_records
GROUP BY
  monthly_records.year
views.description: Aggregate monthly_records to compute the total (sum) delivered orders volume for each year.

views.name: min_year_by_annual_delivered
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  year AS year,
  annual_delivered_orders_volume AS annual_delivered_orders_volume,
  RANK() OVER (ORDER BY annual_delivered_orders_volume ASC) AS annual_rank
FROM annual_delivered_per_year
views.description: Rank or identify the single year among the aggregated years that has the minimum annual_delivered_orders_volume (ties handled per final step). One row per year with its annual total and a rank by annual_delivered_orders_volume ascending.

views.name: monthly_in_min_year
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  m.year AS year,
  m.month AS month,
  m.delivered_orders_volume AS monthly_delivered_orders_volume,
  a.annual_delivered_orders_volume AS annual_delivered_orders_volume
FROM monthly_records AS m
JOIN (
  SELECT year, annual_delivered_orders_volume
  FROM min_year_by_annual_delivered
  WHERE annual_rank = 1
) AS miny ON m.year = miny.year
JOIN annual_delivered_per_year AS a ON m.year = a.year
views.description: Join monthly_records to the single year identified as the minimum from min_year_by_annual_delivered to produce months only from that year, keeping each month's delivered_orders_volume alongside the year's annual_delivered_orders_volume for final selection.

views.name: delivered_orders
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  o.order_id AS order_id,
  c.customer_unique_id AS customer_unique_id,
  o.order_status AS order_status,
  c.customer_city AS order_city,
  c.customer_state AS order_state,
  (op.order_id || '-' || op.payment_sequential) AS payment_id,
  op.payment_value AS payment_value,
  o.order_purchase_timestamp AS order_ts
FROM olist_orders o
JOIN olist_customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
LEFT JOIN olist_order_payments op ON o.order_id = op.order_id
WHERE o.order_status = 'delivered'
views.description: All orders restricted to those with status = 'delivered', keeping order-level fields needed for later joins and aggregations (customer id, order id, city, state, payment id/value, and any timestamp).

views.name: payments_normalized
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  (order_id || '_' || COALESCE(CAST(payment_sequential AS TEXT), '0')) AS payment_id,
  order_id AS order_id,
  COALESCE(CAST(payment_value AS REAL), 0.0) AS payment_value
FROM olist_order_payments
views.description: Normalize/clean payment records so each payment row has a consistent numeric payment_value and links to its order (cast types, handle nulls). One row per payment record suitable for aggregation.

views.name: delivered_order_payments
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  o.order_id AS order_id,
  c.customer_unique_id AS customer_unique_id,
  c.customer_city AS order_city,
  c.customer_state AS order_state,
  p.payment_value AS payment_value
FROM olist_orders o
JOIN olist_customers c
  ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
JOIN olist_order_payments p
  ON o.order_id = p.order_id
WHERE o.order_status = 'delivered'
views.description: Join delivered orders to their normalized payments to produce one row per delivered order-payment pairing, carrying order-level city/state and customer id along with payment value.

views.name: customer_delivered_aggregates
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  c.customer_unique_id AS customer_unique_id,
  COUNT(o.order_id) AS delivered_order_count,
  AVG(p.payment_value) AS average_payment_value,
  -- pick the most frequent city for delivered orders; tie-breaker: MIN(city)
  (SELECT co.customer_city
     FROM olist_orders oo
     JOIN olist_customers co ON oo.customer_id = co.customer_id
     WHERE oo.order_status = 'delivered' AND co.customer_unique_id = c.customer_unique_id
     GROUP BY co.customer_city
     ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC, MIN(co.customer_city) ASC
     LIMIT 1) AS city,
  (SELECT co2.customer_state
     FROM olist_orders oo2
     JOIN olist_customers co2 ON oo2.customer_id = co2.customer_id
     WHERE oo2.order_status = 'delivered' AND co2.customer_unique_id = c.customer_unique_id
     GROUP BY co2.customer_state
     ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC, MIN(co2.customer_state) ASC
     LIMIT 1) AS state
FROM olist_customers c
LEFT JOIN olist_orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id AND o.order_status = 'delivered'
LEFT JOIN olist_order_payments p ON o.order_id = p.order_id
GROUP BY c.customer_unique_id
views.description: For each customer, compute the count of delivered orders and the average payment_value across their delivered orders, and determine a deterministic city and state to represent that customer's delivered-orders (e.g., most frequent city/state among their delivered orders or another consistent tie-breaker). One row per customer.

views.name: orders_with_city_and_status
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  o.order_id AS order_id,
  c.customer_city AS city,
  o.order_status AS order_status
FROM olist_orders o
LEFT JOIN olist_customers c
  ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
views.description: All orders with their associated city and order status (one row per order). This filters/identifies orders and exposes the city to which each order belongs and the order's status.

views.name: payments_by_order
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  order_id || '-' || CAST(payment_sequential AS TEXT) AS payment_id,
  order_id,
  payment_value AS payment_amount
FROM olist_order_payments
views.description: All payment records linked to orders, with the payment amount and the order id for each payment (one row per payment).

views.name: city_payment_and_delivered_counts
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  c.customer_city AS city,
  SUM(op.payment_value) AS total_payments_per_city,
  COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN o.order_status = 'delivered' THEN o.order_id END) AS delivered_order_count_per_city
FROM olist_customers c
JOIN olist_orders o
  ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
LEFT JOIN olist_order_payments op
  ON o.order_id = op.order_id
GROUP BY c.customer_city
views.description: For each city, sum all payment amounts for payments tied to orders in that city and count distinct orders with status = 'delivered' (one row per city). This produces per-city total payments and delivered-order counts; include cities even if delivered count is zero (filtering to >0 happens later).

views.name: select_bottom_five_and_compute_averages
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  AVG(c.total_payments_per_city) AS average_of_total_payments_for_selected_cities,
  AVG(c.delivered_order_count_per_city) AS average_of_delivered_order_counts_for_selected_cities,
  'selection_bucket' AS selection_bucket
FROM (
  SELECT
    city,
    total_payments_per_city,
    delivered_order_count_per_city
  FROM city_payment_and_delivered_counts
  ORDER BY total_payments_per_city ASC
  LIMIT 5
) c
views.description: Rank or order cities by their total payments ascending, select the first five cities, and compute the average of the selected cities' total_payments_per_city and the average of their delivered_order_count_per_city (one row containing the two averages).

views.name: delivered_order_rows
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  oi.seller_id AS seller_id,
  oi.order_id AS order_id,
  c.customer_unique_id AS customer_unique_id,
  oi.price AS price,
  oi.freight_value AS freight_value,
  r.review_score AS review_score
FROM olist_order_items oi
JOIN olist_orders o USING(order_id)
JOIN olist_customers c USING(customer_id)
LEFT JOIN olist_order_reviews r USING(order_id)
WHERE o.order_status = 'delivered'
views.description: Select delivered-order rows only: every order-row/transaction record whose delivery/status indicator denotes delivered. Keep all columns needed for later metrics (seller id, order id, customer unique id, price, freight value, review score).

views.name: seller_order_level_metrics
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  dor.seller_id AS seller_id,
  COUNT(DISTINCT dor.customer_unique_id) AS distinct_customer_count,
  SUM(dor.price - dor.freight_value) AS total_profit,
  COUNT(DISTINCT dor.order_id) AS distinct_order_count,
  SUM(CASE WHEN dor.review_score = 5 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS five_star_count
FROM delivered_order_rows dor
GROUP BY dor.seller_id
views.description: Aggregate delivered order rows to compute per-seller measures needed for ranking: distinct count of customer_unique_id, sum of (price - freight_value) as total_profit, distinct count of order_id, and count of rows where review_score = 5 (five_star_count). Do not pick winners here — produce one row per seller with these metric values.

views.name: seller_metric_rows
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.seller_id,
  metric_name,
  metric_value
FROM olist_sellers s
JOIN (
  SELECT
    seller_id,
    'distinct_customer_count' AS metric_name,
    CAST(distinct_customer_count AS FLOAT) AS metric_value
  FROM seller_order_level_metrics
  UNION ALL
  SELECT
    seller_id,
    'total_profit' AS metric_name,
    CAST(total_profit AS FLOAT) AS metric_value
  FROM seller_order_level_metrics
  UNION ALL
  SELECT
    seller_id,
    'distinct_order_count' AS metric_name,
    CAST(distinct_order_count AS FLOAT) AS metric_value
  FROM seller_order_level_metrics
  UNION ALL
  SELECT
    seller_id,
    'five_star_count' AS metric_name,
    CAST(five_star_count AS FLOAT) AS metric_value
  FROM seller_order_level_metrics
) m ON s.seller_id = m.seller_id
views.description: Unpivot the per-seller metric columns into a long form of metric rows so each row represents one (seller, metric_type, metric_value). This creates comparable rows for each metric type per seller (e.g., 'distinct_customer_count', 'total_profit', 'distinct_order_count', 'five_star_count').

views.name: top_seller_per_metric
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  smr.metric_name AS metric_name,
  smr.seller_id AS seller_id,
  smr.metric_value AS metric_value,
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY smr.metric_name ORDER BY smr.metric_value DESC) AS rank
FROM seller_metric_rows smr
views.description: For each metric_name, rank sellers by metric_value descending and select the top seller(s). Keep ties if the SQL execution chooses RANK semantics; output one row per winning seller-metric with the metric value. (Final query will map metric_name to the human-readable achievement_description.)

views.name: payments_with_product_category
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  olist_order_payments.payment_sequential || '_' || olist_order_payments.order_id AS payment_id,
  olist_order_payments.payment_type AS payment_method,
  olist_products.product_category_name AS product_category,
  olist_order_payments.order_id AS order_id,
  olist_order_payments.payment_value AS payment_value
FROM olist_order_payments
JOIN olist_order_items
  ON olist_order_payments.order_id = olist_order_items.order_id
JOIN olist_products
  ON olist_order_items.product_id = olist_products.product_id
views.description: All payment records joined to the product category of the purchased item so each payment row is annotated with the corresponding product category. Exclude any records that are not payments. Do not aggregate here.

views.name: category_payment_method_counts
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.product_category_name AS product_category,
  op.payment_type AS payment_method,
  COUNT(*) AS payment_count,
  p.product_id,
  op.order_id,
  op.payment_sequential
FROM olist_products p
JOIN olist_order_items i ON i.product_id = p.product_id
JOIN olist_order_payments op ON op.order_id = i.order_id
GROUP BY p.product_category_name, op.payment_type, p.product_id, op.order_id, op.payment_sequential
views.description: Count number of payments grouped by product category and payment method. Produces one row per (category, payment method) with the count of payments for that pair.

views.name: category_top_payment_method
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  cpc.product_category AS product_category,
  -- choose the top payment method per category using row_number tie-broken by lexical payment_method
  pm_top.payment_method AS top_payment_method,
  pm_top.payment_count AS payments_for_top_method
FROM
  (
    SELECT
      product_category,
      payment_method,
      payment_count,
      ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
        PARTITION BY product_category
        ORDER BY payment_count DESC, payment_method ASC
      ) AS rn
    FROM category_payment_method_counts
  ) AS pm_top
  JOIN (
    SELECT DISTINCT product_category FROM category_payment_method_counts
  ) AS cpc
    ON pm_top.product_category = cpc.product_category
WHERE pm_top.rn = 1
views.description: For each product category, rank payment methods by payment_count descending and apply a deterministic tie-breaker (e.g., smallest lexical payment_method or smallest id) so that exactly one payment method is selected per category. Keep only the top-ranked payment method per category along with its payment_count.

views.name: average_of_top_method_counts
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  ctp.product_category AS product_category,
  ctp.top_payment_method AS top_payment_method,
  ctp.payments_for_top_method AS payments_for_top_method,
  -- compute the average across categories (only categories present in category_top_payment_method)
  (SELECT AVG(payments_for_top_method) FROM category_top_payment_method) AS average_payments_across_categories
FROM category_top_payment_method AS ctp
views.description: Compute the single-number average of payments_for_top_method across all categories included (exclude categories that had zero payments and therefore do not appear in the input). Also pass through the per-category top rows so final output can include both per-category fields and the overall average.

views.name: category_payment_counts
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.product_category_name AS product_category,
  op.payment_type AS payment_type,
  COUNT(op.order_id) AS payment_count,
  -- preserve keys for joinability
  p.product_id AS product_id,
  op.order_id AS order_id
FROM olist_products p
JOIN olist_order_items i ON p.product_id = i.product_id
JOIN olist_order_payments op ON i.order_id = op.order_id
GROUP BY
  p.product_category_name,
  op.payment_type,
  p.product_id,
  op.order_id
views.description: Aggregate counts of payments by product category and payment type. One row per category/payment_type with the number of payments using that payment type for that category.

views.name: category_top_payment_types
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  c.product_category AS product_category,
  c.payment_type AS payment_type,
  c.payment_count AS payment_count,
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY c.product_category ORDER BY c.payment_count DESC) AS payment_rank_within_category
FROM (
  SELECT
    op.product_category_name AS product_category,
    p.payment_type AS payment_type,
    COUNT(DISTINCT oi.order_id || '-' || p.payment_type || COALESCE(p.payment_sequential,0)) AS payment_count
  FROM olist_order_items oi
  JOIN olist_products op
    ON oi.product_id = op.product_id
  JOIN olist_order_payments p
    ON oi.order_id = p.order_id
  GROUP BY op.product_category_name, p.payment_type
) c
views.description: For each product category, determine the payment type(s) that are the most common. Rank or mark payment types within each category by payment_count so we can keep ties for the top position.

views.name: top_three_categories_by_payment_count
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  c.product_category AS product_category,
  c.payment_type AS payment_type,
  c.payment_count AS payment_count,
  RANK() OVER (ORDER BY c.payment_count DESC, c.product_category ASC) AS category_rank
FROM (
  SELECT
    category_payment_counts.product_category AS product_category,
    category_payment_counts.payment_type AS payment_type,
    SUM(category_payment_counts.payment_count) AS payment_count
  FROM category_payment_counts
  GROUP BY category_payment_counts.product_category, category_payment_counts.payment_type
) AS c
views.description: From the top payment type(s) per category, compute one row per top payment_type per category and then rank categories by their top payment_count to produce the final ordered/limited result (apply secondary sort by product_category for tie-breaking when limiting to three).

views.name: geolocations_sel
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  row_number() OVER (ORDER BY geolocation_zip_code_prefix, geolocation_state, geolocation_city, geolocation_lat, geolocation_lng) AS geolocation_id,
  geolocation_state,
  geolocation_city,
  geolocation_zip_code_prefix,
  geolocation_lat,
  geolocation_lng
FROM olist_geolocation
WHERE geolocation_lat IS NOT NULL
  AND geolocation_lng IS NOT NULL
views.description: Select all rows from the geolocation source with no additional row-level filtering (aside from later exclusion of null coordinates). This is the raw input relation.

views.name: geolocations_normalized_coords
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  geolocation_id,
  geolocation_state,
  geolocation_city,
  geolocation_zip_code_prefix,
  geolocation_lat,
  geolocation_lng,
  (geolocation_lat * PI() / 180.0) AS lat_rad,
  (geolocation_lng * PI() / 180.0) AS lon_rad
FROM geolocations_sel
WHERE geolocation_lat IS NOT NULL
  AND geolocation_lng IS NOT NULL
views.description: Project and normalize coordinate fields: compute lat/lon in radians from the latitude/longitude degrees, and preserve identifying and ordering columns. Exclude rows where lat or lon is NULL (this is a cleaning step so later pair computations can assume non-null radians).

views.name: geolocations_ordered_win
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  g.geolocation_id,
  g.geolocation_state,
  g.geolocation_city,
  g.geolocation_zip_code_prefix,
  g.geolocation_lat,
  g.geolocation_lng,
  g.lat_rad,
  g.lon_rad,
  LAG(g.geolocation_id) OVER (
    ORDER BY g.geolocation_state, g.geolocation_city, g.geolocation_zip_code_prefix, g.geolocation_lat, g.geolocation_lng
  ) AS prev_geolocation_id,
  LAG(g.geolocation_state) OVER (
    ORDER BY g.geolocation_state, g.geolocation_city, g.geolocation_zip_code_prefix, g.geolocation_lat, g.geolocation_lng
  ) AS prev_geolocation_state,
  LAG(g.geolocation_city) OVER (
    ORDER BY g.geolocation_state, g.geolocation_city, g.geolocation_zip_code_prefix, g.geolocation_lat, g.geolocation_lng
  ) AS prev_geolocation_city,
  LAG(g.geolocation_zip_code_prefix) OVER (
    ORDER BY g.geolocation_state, g.geolocation_city, g.geolocation_zip_code_prefix, g.geolocation_lat, g.geolocation_lng
  ) AS prev_geolocation_zip_code_prefix,
  LAG(g.geolocation_lat) OVER (
    ORDER BY g.geolocation_state, g.geolocation_city, g.geolocation_zip_code_prefix, g.geolocation_lat, g.geolocation_lng
  ) AS prev_geolocation_lat,
  LAG(g.geolocation_lng) OVER (
    ORDER BY g.geolocation_state, g.geolocation_city, g.geolocation_zip_code_prefix, g.geolocation_lat, g.geolocation_lng
  ) AS prev_geolocation_lng,
  LAG(g.lat_rad) OVER (
    ORDER BY g.geolocation_state, g.geolocation_city, g.geolocation_zip_code_prefix, g.geolocation_lat, g.geolocation_lng
  ) AS prev_lat_rad,
  LAG(g.lon_rad) OVER (
    ORDER BY g.geolocation_state, g.geolocation_city, g.geolocation_zip_code_prefix, g.geolocation_lat, g.geolocation_lng
  ) AS prev_lon_rad
FROM geolocations_normalized_coords g
views.description: Order the normalized geolocations by state, city, zip_code_prefix, latitude, longitude and compute the previous-row (lag) values for the id, identifying fields, and radian coordinates so each row is paired with its immediate predecessor in the specified ordering.

views.name: consecutive_pair_distances
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  prev_geolocation_id,
  prev_geolocation_state,
  prev_geolocation_city,
  prev_geolocation_zip_code_prefix,
  prev_geolocation_lat,
  prev_geolocation_lng,
  geolocation_id,
  geolocation_state,
  geolocation_city,
  geolocation_zip_code_prefix,
  geolocation_lat,
  geolocation_lng,
  -- spherical law of cosines: d = R * acos( sin φ1*sin φ2 + cos φ1*cos φ2*cos(Δλ) )
  -- lat/lon in radians already provided by geolocations_ordered_win as lat_rad, lon_rad, prev_lat_rad, prev_lon_rad
  6371.0 * acos(
    -- clamp cosine argument to [-1,1] to avoid domain errors without using LEAST/GREATEST
    CASE
      WHEN (sin(prev_lat_rad) * sin(lat_rad) + cos(prev_lat_rad) * cos(lat_rad) * cos(prev_lon_rad - lon_rad)) > 1.0 THEN 1.0
      WHEN (sin(prev_lat_rad) * sin(lat_rad) + cos(prev_lat_rad) * cos(lat_rad) * cos(prev_lon_rad - lon_rad)) < -1.0 THEN -1.0
      ELSE (sin(prev_lat_rad) * sin(lat_rad) + cos(prev_lat_rad) * cos(lat_rad) * cos(prev_lon_rad - lon_rad))
    END
  ) AS distance_km
FROM geolocations_ordered_win
WHERE prev_geolocation_id IS NOT NULL
views.description: For each row that has a previous-row (i.e., forms a consecutive pair), compute the great-circle distance in kilometers between the row and its predecessor using the spherical law of cosines formula with Earth's radius (distance per-pair). This relation is one row per consecutive pair (identified by the earlier and later geolocation ids).
